title: Does the car leave the road? 40 km/h no, 60 km/h yes: 16 m in the air; the limit is 49.7 km/h
description:
Does the car leave the road? The same humpback bridge twice: a cosine hump 2.5 m high and 31 m long on a flat road, y(x) = (H / 2)(1 + cos(2 pi x / L)) for x from minus L / 2 to plus L / 2, which joins the road with zero slope; its crest radius is R = L^2 / (2 pi^2 H) = 19.4739 m and its steepest slope 14.22 degrees. The car is a point moving along the road at a steady speed (the engine holds the speed; no suspension, so a real car's springs would change the gap, not the limit); g = 9.80665 m/s^2. While the wheels touch, the road pushes up per unit mass with N = g cos(theta) - v^2 kappa, theta the road slope and kappa the convex curvature of the road; the wheels leave where N reaches zero, the car flies on the parabola from its tangent velocity and lands where the parabola meets the road again (the root by bisection); the landing takes the vertical speed and the car runs on along the road at its steady speed. At the crest N = g - v^2 / R, so the limit is sqrt(g R) = 13.8193 m/s = 49.75 km/h, whatever the car weighs. Top panel 40 km/h (11.1111 m/s), bottom panel 60 km/h (16.6667 m/s); stepped at 1e-04 s (RK4 along the road, the leave point by bisection inside the step, the closed-form parabola in the air, the landing by bisection); shown at 1/3 speed on a 10 s cycle, 4 cycles in 40 s. Drawing only: the car body sits on the chord between its two wheel contacts, and in the air its pitch turns evenly from the take-off slope to the landing slope (the point model has no attitude). Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- 40 km/h: the wheels never leave; the road push bottoms at 0.3535 of the car's weight at the crest (1 - v^2 / (g R)); the car passes the crest 1.7771 s after the start and is 17.046 m past it at the cycle end
- 60 km/h: the wheels leave 3.859 m before the crest (road slope 10.12 degrees, 0.9519 s after the start); the car is in the air for 16.206 m and 0.9877 s, at most 0.5060 m (50.6 cm) above the road at 7.989 m past the crest, 0.0546 m above the crest as it passes it (1.1871 s), and lands 12.347 m past the crest at 1.9396 s with 6.757 m/s of downward speed (4.230 m/s into the road); the parabola's apex is 2.5744 m, 0.0744 m above the crest
- the limit between them: sqrt(g R) = 49.75 km/h, about 50 km/h
- 50 km/h (13.8889 m/s): right on the limit; N dips to -0.0101 g at the crest, the wheels leave 0.658 m before the crest and the car is in the air for 2.633 m and 0.1897 s with a gap of at most 0.0004 m, landing 1.976 m past the crest
- 55 km/h (15.2778 m/s): the wheels leave 2.882 m before the crest, the car is in the air for 11.820 m and 0.7812 s, at most 0.1602 m (16.0 cm) above the road, and lands 8.938 m past the crest with 5.547 m/s of downward speed
- 70 km/h (19.4444 m/s): the wheels leave 5.003 m before the crest, the car is in the air for 22.195 m and 1.1676 s, at most 1.3959 m (139.6 cm) above the road, and lands 17.193 m past the crest with 7.361 m/s of downward speed
- the smaller hump of the backlog entry, 1.5 m high and 24 m long: crest radius 19.4537 m, limit 49.72 km/h; at 60 km/h the wheels leave 3.037 m before the crest, the car is in the air for 12.779 m and 0.7742 s, at most 0.3237 m (32.4 cm) above the road, and lands 9.742 m past the crest
- checks: N = 0 solved by bisection on x gives the leave point -3.858788 m, the same as the stepped march (diff +0.0e+00 m); halving the time step to 5e-05 s moves the leave time by +2.1e-14 s and leaves the flight length, the flight time, the largest gap and the landing point unchanged (diffs +0.0e+00); at 40 km/h the smallest push moves by +9.1e-17 and the crest time by +2.7e-12 s

Why: over the crest the road bends away under the car. To follow the bend the car must accelerate downward at v^2 / R, and gravity is all that pulls it down. At 40 km/h gravity has more than enough: the road still has to push up with 0.3535 of the weight to keep the car on the bend. At 49.75 km/h gravity alone makes exactly the bend, so the road pushes with nothing. Faster than that, gravity cannot bend the path as sharply as the road bends, so the car goes straight on and the road drops away under it: at 60 km/h the push reaches zero 3.859 m before the crest, where the road is already curving hard, and the car flies 16.206 m before the road comes back up to meet it. The car's mass cancels out of N = g - v^2 / R, so the limit is the same for any car. A real car's suspension changes how the gap grows, not where the push runs out.
